channel.title: Crypto Readout
channel.description: Crypto Readout reports on Bitcoin, Ethereum and altcoin markets, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, network upgrades and crypto regulation worldwide.

item.title: Why a Bridge Refund Can Need Another Message
item.description: A bridge refund can require a second message because the source chain cannot undo a transfer alone; a verified return instruction must still be delivered and executed.

item.title: What Lock Expiry Does to a Token’s Volatility
item.description: Compare volatility before and after a liquidity lock expires against the token’s own baseline, tracking pool depth, trading volume and the exact unlock time.

item.title: How to Check BSC Token Liquidity Before a Swap
item.description: Before swapping a BSC token, verify its contract, inspect the correct pool’s reserves and compare your trade size with available liquidity to judge price impact.

item.title: ERC-20 Allowances: The Approval Behind a Bridge Deposit
item.description: An ERC-20 approval lets a bridge contract move a set amount of tokens; the deposit call then starts the bridge’s separate source-chain and destination-chain steps.

item.title: Schedule Polygon PoS exits by separating the burn from the claim
item.description: A Polygon PoS exit has a Polygon burn, a validator checkpoint and an Ethereum claim; plan the first early, then submit the claim when Ethereum gas fits your timing and budget.

item.title: Four Decisions That Make Cross-Chain Rate Limits Work
item.description: Cross-chain rate limits work only when teams define what they count, where limits apply, how bursts refill, and what happens to traffic already in flight.

item.title: Why a Source Reorg Cannot Roll Back Every Omnichain Transfer
item.description: A source-chain reorg can erase a transfer after a destination has acted; finality gates, message tracking and recovery rules define the rollback limit.

item.title: Omnichain Message Schemas: The Fields to Check Before Bridging
item.description: An omnichain message schema defines how a bridge labels, encodes, verifies and delivers a cross-chain instruction; matching fields matter as much as matching bytes.

item.title: What a Hardware Wallet Approves in a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A hardware wallet signs the transactions behind a cross-chain swap. Check token permissions, route details and network fees before confirming each step.

item.title: Why a 100 USDC Bridge Quote May Deliver Less
item.description: A bridge quote estimates what reaches the destination after route fees, swaps and slippage; check which costs it includes before approving the transfer.

item.title: Three Checks for Monero Deposits After a Reorg
item.description: After a Monero reorg, verify the deposit’s block is canonical, rescan the receiving wallet, and confirm the output is still present and unlocked before treating it as settled.

item.title: How to test an XMR bridge transfer with ZeroFi
item.description: ZeroFi’s test bridge pairs Sepolia ETH with real Monero, so a useful trial checks the wallet setup, deposit, zXMR mint and return path with a very small amount.

item.title: What a TRON token approval lets a swap contract do
item.description: A TRC-20 approval lets a swap contract spend a set amount of tokens; frequent traders can choose between repeat approvals, capped allowances and lasting access.

item.title: What Front-Running Can Cost a TRON Swap Beginner
item.description: A TRON swap can lose value when a bot trades around a pending order; pool depth, transaction ordering and slippage limits shape the loss or failure.

item.title: Four Checks for Stablecoin Pool Impact on TRON
item.description: Stablecoin pools can quote near-par swaps, but imbalance, route choice and fees change what arrives. Check four details before signing a TRON swap.

item.title: How to Choose a Route for Repeat Cross-Chain Transfers
item.description: For repeat transfers, compare the asset received, total cost, settlement time and route mechanics; the lowest quoted fee may not be the cheapest reliable choice.

item.title: How Unequal Assets Fund a Liquidity Position
item.description: Unequal tokens can still fund a liquidity position, but the pool's price and range determine the required mix, any conversion, and the risks left behind.

item.title: Why a Bridge Deposit Can Change Status After a Reorg
item.description: A bridge deposit can lose confirmations when its source chain replaces recent blocks; check the transaction, bridge rule and destination state before retrying.

item.title: A bridge screen is not proof that a transfer happened
item.description: A bridge screen can show a convincing animation without moving funds; verify each wallet request and both chain records to tell a real transfer from a staged one.

item.title: What Minimum Received Means on a Crypto Swap
item.description: Minimum received sets the lowest output a swap will accept; see how the quote, slippage tolerance and router check work, and when a trade will revert.
